title: Event log retention as an operational switching cost
text: Sehgal argues that an AI agent's operational continuity resides in its durable event history—the recorded sequence of prompts, retrieved context, tool calls, and user interventions—rather than in the runtime or model executing it. Consequently, log ownership can become an important switching cost: if an organization cannot inspect, export, or replay this operational history, migrating an agent workflow can complicate reproducing its path-dependent behavior and accumulated context. (Adapted as an architectural pillar in Ismail's manuscript, S42).
qualification: Vendor-origin architectural argument and position paper by the founder of Omnara (an open-source agent command center), also delivered as an AI Engineer World's Fair keynote. Proposes treating append-only event logs as the persistent definition of an agent rather than models or runtime infrastructure. Retaining, redacting, and replaying extensive agent telemetry creates substantial data-governance, storage, and privacy overhead in enterprise settings.
